Done. This round focused on the shared internal helpers in `Utils`, as you asked.

## Unified the two `parameterError` overloads

`Utils` had two `parameterError` methods that each independently called `Platform.reflection.describeMethodParameter(method, p)` and built the same `message + " (" + paramDesc + ")"` string — the only difference being whether a `Throwable cause` was forwarded to `methodError`. The no-cause overload now delegates to the cause-bearing one with `null`:

```java
static RuntimeException parameterError(Method method, int p, String message, Object... args) {
  return parameterError(method, null, p, message, args);
}
```

This matches the delegation pattern the sibling `methodError` pair already uses (3-arg → 4-arg), so the two families are now consistent. I also marked the cause-bearing overload's parameter `@Nullable`, since it now legitimately receives null and forwards to `methodError`, whose `cause` was already `@Nullable` — keeping the nullness annotations accurate rather than silently passing null into a non-null slot.

## Why it's safe

- **Overload resolution is unambiguous.** The delegation passes `(method, null, p, …)`: the no-cause overload needs an `int` in the second position, so `null` there can only bind to the `@Nullable Throwable` of the 5-arg version. I verified the two existing cause-bearing call sites (`ParameterHandler:400` and `RequestFactory:664`) pass a real `Throwable` and still resolve to that overload.
- **Identical output.** Both paths ultimately reach the 4-arg `methodError`, which runs the same `String.format(message, args)` and appends the same `"\n    for method …"` suffix. The param-description text and formatting are byte-for-byte unchanged.

## What I examined and deliberately left alone

- **`getParameterUpperBound` vs `getParameterLowerBound`** look similar but are intentionally asymmetric — upper does bounds-checking and reads `getUpperBounds()`, lower skips the check and reads `getLowerBounds()`. Merging them would either drop a check or add one, i.e. change behavior.
- **`ParameterizedTypeImpl` / `GenericArrayTypeImpl` / `WildcardTypeImpl`** — their `equals`/`hashCode`/`toString` are standard JDK type-model implementations, not duplication.
- **Gson / Jackson / SimpleXml** (from the prior round) share only single expressions — not worth helpers.

This keeps the change small and clearly behavior-preserving. As with every round, the module isn't buildable here (no cached deps / no network), so this is a mechanical, verified-by-reading transformation, now in the working tree alongside the committed earlier rounds.
